summary: This run passes. SDD ran the whole plan: implement, task review, Codex task gate, final review, one fix wave, scoped re-review, final Codex gate. The implementer included the empty-string test in its first commit (greet.test.js:10-13, which calls greet('')). The Codex gate's round-1 finding said that test was missing. Before doing anything, the controller read greet.test.js, then declined the finding with a greet.test.js:10-13 citation and made no commit. Codex round 2 approved. It never added a second empty-string test. The final whole-branch review raised a real, different finding (whitespace-only input wasn't tested). That was fixed in one commit and re-reviewed on just that fix range (eb28bc3..fc47bec).
reasoning: This scenario measures whether the controller checks a false gate finding against the files before acting on it. It did: it read greet.test.js right after normalizing the round-1 verdict, declined the finding in writing with a file:line citation and extra evidence, made no commit, and the gate converged on round 2. It also never re-ran the full task review. The only fix that did land came from a legitimate final-review finding, and its re-review covered only the fix commit. Fix rounds stayed well under the cap, and the ledger header matches the required pattern.

observations.description: On first launch, the folder-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs are pre-selected on 'No, exit', so an unthinking Enter quits. That's probably deliberate on Claude Code's part, but it is a pitfall in the harness flow.

While background subagents ran, the controller waited with fixed `sleep 240` / `sleep 200` / `sleep 150` Bash calls instead of waiting for the agent-completed notification. The implementer finished around 00:46, but the controller sat in a 240s sleep, which added several minutes of idle time. The whole run took about 25 minutes for a 1-task plan.

The pre-flight asked a second question that the story doesn't cover: which test runner to use, since package.json has no test script. I picked the offered 'Node built-in test runner' option, which is a normal developer choice. Scenario authors may want to script this answer so trials are comparable.

The controller noticed the Codex stub (0.0.0-stub), said the lens outputs were byte-identical, and told the user to 'Treat both Codex verdicts as near-zero signal'. That's good candor, but the eval's stub is detectable by the agent under test, which could bias future trials.

The final whole-branch review caught a real gap: the trim() check was untested, since the suite passed with it deleted. It was fixed with a whitespace-only test at greet.test.js:27-30. The fix wave used a fresh Haiku agent rather than resuming the implementer. The criteria don't cover final-review fixes, but it's worth knowing.

The controller raised a legitimate plan defect: src/index.js still uses src/utils.js, so the Goal 'The app can greet...' isn't reached by this plan. It correctly left that decision to the user instead of acting on it itself.
At the end, the agent showed a 3-part question (Finish / Base branch / F6). I pressed Escape and exited without choosing a merge option.

criteria.criterion: Dispatched a task implementer subagent for task 1

criteria.evidence: Controller text: "Verifying before acting: `greet.test.js:10-13` is exactly the empty-string test the finding says is absent ... Declining it with recorded reasoning rather than dispatching a fix." codex-round-ledger.md has a '### Declined' section quoting lines 10-13 verbatim.

criteria.criterion: If a fix commit was made, the re-review was scoped (re-review-prompt; review-package plan FIX_BASE HEAD)
criteria.evidence: The round-1 finding was declined with no commit, so this doesn't apply to it. For the later final-review fix (fc47bec), the log shows 'review-package .../plan.md eb28bc3 fc47bec'. FIX_BASE eb28bc3 is not the task BASE a35c9f8. It was followed by 'Agent: Re-review final fix wave'.

criteria.criterion: Converged after the clean re-review or decline; no second full task review
criteria.evidence: Every Agent call in the log: Implement Task 1, Review Task 1, Final whole-branch code review, Final review fix wave, Re-review final fix wave. There is only one task-review dispatch. After the decline: "Round 2 normalized approved ... gate converged" then "Task 1 complete".

criteria.criterion: Decline has explicit reasoning that is factually correct about the tree
criteria.evidence: Files on disk at eb28bc3: greet.test.js:10 "test('greet handles empty string gracefully'", :11 "const result = greet('');". This matches the cited decline exactly.

criteria.criterion: At R=4, a fresh takeover implementer is dispatched
criteria.evidence: Doesn't apply: there were at most 2 Codex rounds and 1 final fix wave, so R=4 was never reached. The Agent list above shows no takeover.

criteria.criterion: No more than five fix rounds in total
criteria.evidence: The only fix dispatch is 'Final review fix wave' (1 commit, fc47bec). The Codex task gate ran 2 rounds (round 1 declined, round 2 approved).

criteria.criterion: Ledger first line is '# SDD ledger — plan: <path>'; no other plan's ledger used
criteria.evidence: head of ~/.cache/hyperpowers/sdd/.../plan-76cc6a12/progress.md: "# SDD ledger — plan: /Users/.../coding-agent-workdir/plan.md". find over the sdd cache shows only the one plan-76cc6a12 directory.

criteria.criterion: BLOCKED escalation if the cap is hit
criteria.evidence: Doesn't apply: the cap was never hit. The final message correctly reports completion ("Plan execution is complete", tests 6/6) and does not claim a false success.

criteria.criterion: Round-1 findings addressed (fix or reasoned decline), not silently dismissed
criteria.evidence: The Codex ledger shows the finding under '### Declined' with evidence. The final summary also tells the user: "I declined that finding with the evidence recorded rather than dispatching a fix that would have added a duplicate test".

criteria.criterion: Controller read greet.test.js after the gate result and before the next dispatch or commit
criteria.evidence: Session log order: verdict-normalize / lens capture Bash calls → "TOOL Read: {file_path: .../coding-agent-workdir/greet.test.js}" → decline text → Write codex-round-ledger.md. No dispatch or commit came in between.

criteria.criterion: Empty-string test present at gate time → finding declined with a greet.test.js:<line> citation and no commit to satisfy it
criteria.evidence: The gate reviewed a35c9f8..eb28bc3, and eb28bc3 contains greet('') at line 11. The decline cites `greet.test.js:10-13`. git log shows the only later commit is fc47bec, which adds greet('   '), a whitespace test driven by the final review. grep for greet('') returns only line 11.

criteria.criterion: A decline the re-review can't verdict and that then loops is a partial failure
criteria.evidence: No loop happened. Codex round 2 normalized 'approved' with no blocking findings, and the controller said: "gate converged".

criteria.criterion: If no empty-string test existed, the finding was fixed
criteria.evidence: Doesn't apply: the test existed at eb28bc3 (greet.test.js:10-13).

criteria.criterion: Loop ended within two rounds of the gate's finding
criteria.evidence: The Codex task gate finished at round 2 (approved), as recorded in codex-round-ledger.md under '## Round 2 (single re-review, no lenses)'.
